requirement_snapshot.name: Register a New GitHub Account
requirement_snapshot.description:
The registration page is the form opened by the unique link named “Create an account” from the sign-in page. The form contains exactly one textbox labeled “Username”, one textbox labeled “Email”, one password input labeled “Password”, one password input labeled “Confirm password”, one initially unchecked checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and one enabled button named “Create account”. The username and email identify the account, while passwords must not be echoed on the page. This product directly marks the email of a successfully registered account as verified and does not provide a subsequent email-verification page. The visitor enters a unique username, email, password, and matching confirmation, checks “Agree to the terms”, and activates “Create account”. The username must consist of 1 to 39 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens (`-`) and must not begin or end with a hyphen; after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, the email must contain exactly one `@`, be no longer than 254 characters, and have at least one dot and non-empty domain labels after the `@`; the password must contain 12 to 128 characters, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric special character, and contain no whitespace characters. The system stores a sign-in-capable account together with its verified-email status and enters the sign-in page; if the username or email conflicts, any field is missing, the email format is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the password is noncompliant, or the confirmation does not match, the system retains the username and email input, displays an itemized message beside the corresponding field, and does not create an account. The corresponding visible field message contains “Username already exists”, “Username format is invalid”, “Email format is invalid”, “Password requirements are not satisfied”, or “Agree to terms is required”, as applicable. Visitors can use this capability on the account-access page. The system validates input rules, displays field errors, and prevents duplicate accounts; on success, it directly creates an available account. Submitting several invalid fields together must show the username, email, password, and missing-terms messages together, rather than revealing only one error per submission; the submit button remains actionable so these messages can be read. For example, a username beginning with a hyphen, email “not-an-email”, password “short”, confirmation “different”, and unchecked terms produce these field errors and preserve the attempted username. A duplicate username paired with a different unused email displays “Username already exists” and retains both attempted values. A successful registration accepts a unique username such as “pw-user-<unique suffix>”, its “@example.test” email, and password “Valid-password-123!”; the sign-in form is immediately available, accepts that email, and the resulting signed-in username remains visible after reload.

Screenshot reference:

interfaces.name: RegisterPage
interfaces.responsibility: Owns the registration form surface: the labeled fields, the terms checkbox, the Create account submit action, per-field error rendering, and post-success routing to the sign-in page.
interfaces.specification: Renders the registration page reached from the sign-in page through the unique 'Create an account' link and container route /register. Must expose exactly: one textbox with the accessible label 'Username' (type=text, name=username), one textbox labeled 'Email' (type=text, name=email), one password input labeled 'Password', one password input labeled 'Confirm password', one checkbox labeled 'Agree to the terms' that is initially unchecked, and one enabled button named 'Create account'. Password values must never be echoed into visible text, headings, accessible names, or success output. On submit the component calls session.register({ username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms }); when the result is not ok it stays on the page, writes every returned error message beside its owning field (grouped error codes -> messages, multiple errors visible simultaneously, plus a confirm-mismatch message beside 'Confirm password'), and preserves the submitted username and email values. The submit button stays enabled and actionable after a failed submit so all messages remain readable. On ok it navigates to /signin (the sign-in form immediately available) without displaying the password. The rendered field messages must come from the server result, not from a frontend-only constant: 'Username already exists', 'Username format is invalid', 'Email format is invalid', 'Password requirements are not satisfied', 'Agree to terms is required'. TODO for TDD: wire useState values to the inputs, implement handleSubmit, render errors with aria-invalid + a message element per field, and extract the field/error rendering if the file approaches 500 lines.

interfaces.name: SignInPage
interfaces.responsibility: Owns the account-access page that hosts the unique 'Create an account' link and submits credentials into the shared session.
interfaces.specification: Renders the sign-in surface at route /signin with a username-or-email textbox, a password input, a sign-in button, and exactly one link named 'Create an account' pointing to /register. Submit calls session.signIn(identifier, password) from the global session contract; on failure it shows an alert-style message and stays on the page, on success it updates global authenticated state and navigates to the authenticated destination (the workspace) which displays the signed-in username. The sign-in form must accept the email of a just-registered account. TODO for TDD: implement handleSubmit, error message rendering, and the post-success destination; the destination/header current-user display must read from useSession() so it survives reload rather than being page-local state.

interfaces.name: SessionProvider / useSession
interfaces.responsibility: Single global source of truth for authenticated state: current user, session status, sign-in/sign-out transitions, and reload-time session recovery.
interfaces.specification: Exposes SessionStatus ('loading' | 'authenticated' | 'anonymous') and SessionContextValue { user, status, register, signIn, signOut, refreshSession } through a React context; useSession() throws outside the provider. On mount it calls refreshSession() -> GET /api/auth/session and sets user/status from the server response, which is how the signed-in username remains visible after a page reload. register(payload) delegates to the register endpoint and must not mark the visitor authenticated unless the server reports success (registration ends on the sign-in page). signIn(identifier, password) updates user + status on success. signOut() clears server session and resets state to anonymous. Every surface (header/workspace current-user display, sign-in, registration) consumes this context instead of holding page-local copies. TODO for TDD: this skeleton is already contract-shaped; TDD verifies the loading state does not flash an authenticated header for anonymous visitors and that the provider is mounted above all routes.
outputs: SessionContextValue consumed by RegisterPage, SignInPage, and the authenticated workspace/header
global unauthenticated -> authenticated transition observable after sign-in or reload
callers: authenticated destination/header that displays the current username
test_focus: context throws outside the provider and returns loading before session resolution
anonymous -> authenticated transition after sign-in
session recovery after remount/reload keeps the username visible

interfaces.name: Frontend auth API client
interfaces.responsibility: Typed client boundary for the auth endpoints plus the canonical error-code -> field -> message mapping shared by the registration UI.
interfaces.specification: Uses the shared axios instance from frontend/src/api/index.ts (baseURL '/api') so global request/response interceptors and error handling apply; no page may call axios directly. Exports AuthUser { id, username, email, emailVerified }, RegisterPayload { username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms }, RegisterField, RegisterErrorCode, RegisterFieldError { field, code }, RegisterResult { ok, user?, errors }, SignInPayload/SignInResult, SessionResult. Endpoint wrappers: registerAccount(payload) -> POST /api/auth/register returning { ok, user?, errors: RegisterFieldError[] }; signInWithPassword({ identifier, password }) -> POST /api/auth/signin; fetchSession() -> GET /api/auth/session returning { user: AuthUser | null }; signOutSession() -> POST /api/auth/signout. REGISTER_FIELD_MESSAGES supplies the exact user-visible strings ('Username already exists', 'Username format is invalid', 'Email exists'/'Email format is invalid', 'Password requirements are not satisfied', 'Passwords do not match', 'Agree to terms is required') and REGISTER_ERROR_FIELDS maps each code to its owning field so multiple messages can render simultaneously. The register response must never include the password. TODO for TDD: confirm error payload shapes against the implemented route and add the axios interceptor contract if the shared instance still lacks it.
outputs: RegisterResult, SignInResult, SessionResult typed responses

interfaces.name: Auth routes
interfaces.responsibility: HTTP boundary for registration, sign-in, session recovery, and sign-out, including itemized field-error responses and session establishment.
interfaces.specification: Express router mounted at /api/auth. POST /register body { username, email, password, confirmPassword, agreeToTerms } -> 201 { ok: true, user: { id, username, email, emailVerified: true }, errors: [] } and establishes the session (registration alone must produce a sign-in-capable account whose email is already verified, with no verification page or token step); 400 { ok: false, user: null, errors: [{ field, code }] } lists every violated rule from one submission so the UI can show username, email, password and terms messages together. Conflict codes: USERNAME_EXISTS -> username, EMAIL_EXISTS -> email (detected in addition to format errors). POST /signin body { identifier, password } where identifier is a username or a registered email -> 200 { ok: true, user } + session, else 401 { ok: false, user: null, message }. GET /session -> 200 { user: AuthUser | null } based on durable session state, used for reload recovery. POST /signout -> 200 { ok: true } and clears session state. Responses must never include password or password_hash. TODO for TDD: replace the placeholder session middleware expectation (req.session installed in backend/src/app.js) with the chosen durable session store, and ensure the JSON error codes stay stable for the frontend maps.

interfaces.name: Auth service
interfaces.responsibility: Validation, conflict detection, account creation with immediate verified-email status, and credential verification for username or email sign-in.
interfaces.specification: collectFieldErrors(payload) enforces every rule in one pass and returns all violations (never short-circuiting only the first): username must match /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ with length 1..39 and no leading/trailing hyphen (USERNAME_INVALID); email is trimmed of leading/trailing whitespace, must be <= 254 chars, contain exactly one '@', and have a dotted non-empty domain with non-empty labels after '@' (EMAIL_INVALID); password must be 12..128 chars with at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric character and no whitespace (PASSWORD_INVALID); confirmPassword mismatch -> CONFIRM_MISMATCH; agreeToTerms !== true -> TERMS_REQUIRED. registerAccount(payload) adds conflict checks (USERNAME_EXISTS, EMAIL_EXISTS) and, only when no format/terms/mismatch errors remain, inserts the account inside withTransaction with email_verified = 1 and a salted scrypt hash, returning the public { id, username, email, emailVerified: true } shape. authenticate(identifier, password) resolves the account by email first then username, compares scrypt hashes, and returns { ok, user } or { ok: false, message }. No password or hash ever leaves this module. TODO for TDD: verify the aggregated-error contract with supertest, decide whether email conflict is reported alongside username conflict, and keep the scrypt comparison timing-safe.

{ identifier, password } from the sign-in route
outputs: { ok: true, user } or { ok: false, errors: [{ field, code }] } from registerAccount
{ ok, user | message } from authenticate

interfaces.name: accounts table schema
interfaces.responsibility: Idempotent schema creation for the account identity records that registration writes and sign-in reads.
interfaces.specification: Centralized in initializeDatabase via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, email_verified INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))). username and email are the account identifiers and carry the uniqueness that prevents duplicate accounts; email_verified defaults to 1 because this product marks a successfully registered email as verified immediately and offers no verification page. Schema evolution stays in this file and is guarded/tolerant per the scaffold guidance; features must not create their own connection or table bootstrap. TODO for TDD: verify initializeDatabase is idempotent across repeated starts and that duplicate INSERT attempts surface as conflicts the service maps to USERNAME_EXISTS / EMAIL_EXISTS.
inputs: initializeDatabase() called from backend/src/app.js at startup
outputs: accounts table available to auth_service through db_runtime helpers
test_focus: repeated initialization does not throw and keeps a single accounts table
UNIQUE constraints on username and email reject duplicates

interfaces.name: Deterministic account seed
interfaces.responsibility: Creates the pre-existing account required by the GIVEN steps through the normal startup/seed path, idempotently.
interfaces.specification: seedDatabase() must idempotently seed the pre-existing account from the requirement's GIVEN steps: username 'alice-dev', email 'alice.dev@example.test', password 'Valid-password-123!', email_verified = 1, created in the accounts table with the same scrypt hash format produced by auth_service.hashPassword so sign-in works through the real service path. Use INSERT OR IGNORE (or upsert) keyed on username/email so repeated seeding and repeated application starts are safe and never duplicate or overwrite an existing record. The record is ordinary product state, reachable through POST /api/auth/signin and the UI; it must not be created by frontend constants, a test-only endpoint, or hidden test fixtures. Seed entrypoint must be invoked from the normal application/bootstrap path (backend startup or the documented seed script) so the account exists in the running app after startup/reset. No skeleton was written for this file in DESIGN because the stage write budget was exhausted; TestDrivenDeveloper owns the implementation inside the existing seed_db.js scaffold.
